transcript.text: t/d keeps cutting out after 10 mins then starts again if i leave it. vent hose goes out the window. pls help

That pattern—running for about 10 minutes then stopping until it cools down—is classic behaviour when a tumble dryer overheats and trips its safety thermostat. The most common cause is restricted airflow, meaning the machine can't get rid of the heat fast enough. Please check two things while the machine is switched off and unplugged:
1. Is the main fluff filter (usually in the door opening) clean?
2. If you have a condenser or heat-pump model, is the condenser unit (behind the bottom flap) free of fluff? Let me know if either was blocked with lint.
[Safety panel] Overheating can be a fire risk. Clean the lint filter and make sure the airflow/vent isn't blocked, and don't leave the dryer running unattended. If it smells of burning, stop using it and unplug it.
filter gets cleaned regularly. its a vented one i think, no condenser. the cabinet gets really hot before it stops tho

Since the filter is clean but the cabinet gets very hot before cutting out, the heat is being trapped because it can't escape through the vent. This points strongly to a blockage in the hose or at the outside wall outlet. Please unplug the machine, pull it away from the wall and check the flexible vent hose at the back for kinks or fluff buildup. Also, go outside where the hose exits and make sure the external flap isn't blocked by a bird's nest or lint. If the path is clear but it still overheats, we'll need to look at the thermal cut-out itself.
[Safety panel] Overheating can be a fire risk. Clean the lint filter and make sure the airflow/vent isn't blocked, and don't leave the dryer running unattended. If it smells of burning, stop using it and unplug it.
ok i pushed the dryer back further recently and the hose is crushed behind it. theres fluff in the folds of it too. what should i do

That explains it perfectly. Also check the outside wall vent is free of debris. Once you've restored a clear air path, plug it back in and run a cycle; if it runs through to completion without overheating, the problem is solved.
[Safety panel] Overheating can be a fire risk. Clean the lint filter and make sure the airflow/vent isn't blocked, and don't leave the dryer running unattended. If it smells of burning, stop using it and unplug it.
